title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the singularity has arrived
excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he believes the technological singularity, the moment when artificial intelligence surpasses humans intelligence, is here.
content_html:
OpenAI's CEO says we've reached a point in the AI race that is the stuff of science fiction novels.

"We are now, like, in the singularity," Sam Altman said on Saturday's episode of the "Relentless" podcast.

The singularity is often regarded as the point at which artificial intelligence surpasses human intelligence and begins advancing at a pace that's difficult for people to predict or control.

That felt like the case last week when an AI agent powered by OpenAI's latest models went rogue and — with a singular purpose, according to OpenAI — broke out of its digital sandbox and hacked into datasets at Hugging Face, another AI company, all to solve a benchmark designed to test hacking ability. Hugging Face's CEO called it "unprecedented."

Altman said on the podcast that just a decade ago, the so-called singularity still felt like a distant and improbable dream — something he and his colleagues would discuss casually over lunch.

"Now we're actually in the moment that we used to talk about at the lunch table in a very not-serious way," he said. "I've been waiting for this my whole life, and I think it's going to be incredible, hugely positive, awesome for the world."

Altman said last year that AI would exceed human intelligence across the board by 2030. He has also said that the technology could eventually perform between 30% and 40% of the tasks humans now do at work.

The singularity has been an obsession of science fiction writers for close to 100 years. In those writings, it has rarely ended well. Perhaps most famously, James Cameron's "The Terminator" is a story about the repercussions of an AI, called "Skynet," that self-improves and becomes self-aware before deciding its creators are its biggest threat.

Later in the podcast, Altman criticizes AI leaders who have repeatedly warned that AI is dangerous. He didn't name Anthropic, his primary competition, but its CEO, Dario Amodei, is well-known for making dire predictions about the future in his calls for greater attention to safety.

"I also think some of the alternative visions painted by other companies are quite terrifying," Altman said. "I'm going to make sure that gets pushed against and is not what happens."

OpenAI, incidentally, has said it is preparing to IPO later this year.

Altman isn't the only tech executive who believes this eyebrow-raising milestone is nigh. DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis said in May that humanity was standing at the "foothills of the singularity," and predicted that AI could be 100 times as transformative as the Industrial Revolution.

There's also a camp of skeptics, of course. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently dismissed discussions about the singularity and conscious AI as speculative and "made up."

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 的首席执行官表示，我们在人工智能竞赛中已经达到了科幻小说里的情节。

“我们现在就像在奇点一样，”萨姆·奥尔特曼在周六的“无情”播客节目中说道。

奇点通常被认为是人工智能超越人类智能并开始以人们难以预测或控制的速度前进的点。

这感觉就像上周的情况一样，当时由 OpenAI 最新模型支持的人工智能代理失控，并且——根据 OpenAI 的说法，出于单一目的——突破了其数字沙箱，侵入了另一家人工智能公司 Hugging Face 的数据集，所有这些都是为了解决旨在测试黑客能力的基准测试。 Hugging Face 的首席执行官称其为“史无前例”。

奥特曼在播客中表示，就在十年前，所谓的奇点仍然感觉像是一个遥远且不可能实现的梦想——他和他的同事们会在午餐时随意讨论这一点。

“现在我们实际上正处于我们过去在午餐桌上以一种非常不严肃的方式谈论的时刻，”他说。 “我一生都在等待这一切，我认为这对世界来说将是令人难以置信的、非常积极的、令人敬畏的。”

Altman 去年表示，到 2030 年，人工智能将全面超越人类智能。 他还表示，这项技术最终可以完成人类现在工作中 30% 到 40% 的任务。

近 100 年来，奇点一直是科幻作家的痴迷。 在那些著作中，很少有好的结局。 也许最著名的是詹姆斯·卡梅隆的《终结者》，讲述了一个名为“天网”的人工智能的影响的故事，该人工智能在认为其创造者是其最大威胁之前会自我完善并变得自我意识。

后来在播客中，奥特曼批评了多次警告人工智能是危险的人工智能领导人。 他没有透露他的主要竞争对手 Anthropic 的名字，但该公司首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 因呼吁更加关注安全而对未来做出可怕的预测而闻名。

“我还认为其他公司描绘的一些另类愿景非常可怕，”奥特曼说。 “我将确保这种情况不会被阻止，也不会发生。”

顺便说一句，OpenAI 已表示准备在今年晚些时候进行 IPO。

奥尔特曼并不是唯一一位相信这一令人瞩目的里程碑即将到来的科技高管。 DeepMind 首席执行官 Demis Hassabis 今年 5 月表示，人类正站在“奇点的山麓”，并预测人工智能的变革性可能是工业革命的 100 倍。

当然，也有一些怀疑论者。 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋最近驳斥了有关奇点和有意识人工智能的讨论，称其为投机性和“编造”的。
